Stonehill football falls to Ohio 35-7 in non-conference road game
Stonehill fell to Ohio by a score of 35-7 on Sept.26 at Peden Stadium. Key performances included Christopher Gill's first career interception and Jack O'Connell's milestone touchdown pass.
The Stonehill football team lost to Ohio by a score of 35-7 at Peden Stadium in Athens, Ohio, on Sept. 26. The Skyhawks are now 1-4 overall and remain 1-0 in the Northeast Conference, while the Bobcats improve to 2-2 for the season.
Christopher Gill recorded his first career interception in the first half after Tyler Bannon hurried the quarterback and deflected the pass. Bannon finished with five tackles during the game. Ma'Hkai Wilson and Gene Townsel each led Stonehill with nine tackles.
Quarterback Jack O'Connell completed 11 of 18 passes for 117 yards and one touchdown, moving into a sixth-place tie with Anton Stoneking at 31 career touchdowns and ranking eighth all-time at Stonehill with 3,515 passing yards. Cole Clarke caught five passes for a total of 64 yards, including a key 32-yard touchdown reception on fourth down that tied the game early in the second quarter.
Ohio took an early lead late in the first quarter on an 18-yard rushing touchdown by Matt Vezza. After Stonehill tied it up, Victor Rosa scored twice for Ohio—a four-yard run before halftime and a six-yard run in the fourth quarter—while Vezza added another rushing touchdown as well as a passing score to Dom Dorwart from 42 yards out.
Logan Chenette punted six times for an average of 41.5 yards per kick, including one punt that traveled 50 yards.
Stonehill will have a bye next week before returning to action against Sacred Heart on Saturday, Oct. 10.
